Whether the assessee must deduct TDS under s.194A/194C/194-I/194J for the year: firm/LLP/company always (rules.deductor.firm); individual/HUF only if previous-year business turnover exceeded rules.deductor.individual_huf_prev_year_turnover_paise -- never assumed from the current year's books alone.
Ledgers under 'Duties & Taxes' whose name contains 'tds' (case-insensitive) -- a books figure only; existence or absence of such a ledger is not itself a conclusion about TDS compliance.

limits_text: Books only: the contract's nature, any lower/nil-deduction certificate (s.197) and, for 194C, a s.194C(6) declaration (own-account transporter, PAN furnished, ten or fewer goods carriages) are not visible from vouchers -- contract nature and any certificate/declaration are a CA judgement call, not a books fact.
s.40(a)(ia) disallows 30% of the sum on TDS default; the second proviso removes this if the payee's Form 26A (Rule 31ACB) shows the income was returned -- s.201(1A) interest still runs either way.
ask_client_text: Confirm the nature of the contract/service and whether any lower/nil-deduction certificate or s.194C(6) declaration applies.
If no TDS was deducted, confirm whether Form 26A is available for this payee.

findings.title_text: Deductor status depends on previous-year turnover
limits_text: An individual/HUF is a s.194A/194C/194-I/194J deductor only if the immediately preceding year's business turnover exceeded ₹1 crore; the current year's books alone cannot establish this.
